Study Buddy
Black holes are incredibly dense regions where gravity is so strong that nothing,
not even light, can escape.
The boundary around them, called the event horizon, is the point of no return—once
crossed, everything is pulled inward.
They form when massive stars collapse and can grow larger by swallowing nearby
matter or merging with other black holes.

Here’s what you’ve studied so far:
Black Holes
Extremely dense objects whose gravity is so strong that not even light can
escape.
The event horizon marks the “point of no return,” where spacetime is
dramatically warped.
They form from the collapse of massive stars and can grow by merging or
accreting matter.
